summary: The root نكف (nkf) primarily means to abstain from or refuse something due to disdain or pride. It implies a sense of haughtiness in declining an action or object.
lane: 1 نَكِفَ مِنَالشَّىْءِ ذ , aor. نَكَفَ ; inf. n. نَكَفٌ ; and نَكَفَ , aor. نَكُفَ ; and ; He abstained from, or refused to do, the thing, from disdain and pride. (Msb.)

تَنَكَّفَ بِمَوْضِعِ كَ َا [ He waited, &c.,] i. q. تَلَيَّثَ. (TA in art. صقر, from the “ Nawádir. ”)
اِسْتَنْكَفَ مِنْهُ (KL, * MA) He disdained, or scorned, it; was ashamed of it. (KL, MA.) See 1.

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
